brainstorming: Explore intent and requirements before building: new features where what to build is still open, or architecture changes. Use for 'how should we build X'.
casual-message: Write a short casual message in the sender's own voice (WhatsApp reply, DM) in a copyable block.
ci-ssh-deploy-timeout: Diagnose CI deploys that intermittently fail with SSH timeouts or connection refused, before touching firewall rules; applies a connect-only retry fix.
commit: Create conventional git commits from staged changes (single or multi-repo). Add 'push' to push too; a plain commit never pushes.
commit-invoice-generator: Turn git commit history into billable invoice line items with estimated hours.
condense-claude-md: Shrink a bloated CLAUDE.md or similar instruction file in place by cutting verbose, redundant and discoverable content.
condense-task-doc: Shrink a bloated task doc (current.md) in place: collapse narratives into tables, drop duplicates, split oversized docs.
continue-session: Produce a copy-paste prompt that starts a fresh session where this one stopped (doc path, next goal, uncommitted state).
design-handoff: Write a brief for someone else to design a screen (external designer, contractor): purpose, audience, rules, measured failures, no design decisions.
doc-to-md: Convert a Word, PDF or Excel file to Markdown so it can be read, searched and diffed in git.
docx-red-edits: Edit someone else's Word file with every change shown in red (deletions struck through), keeping their formatting intact.
done: Post-task wrap-up: simplify code, review changes, design-review changed screens, update docs, capture lessons. Use when finished or the user says 'done'.
emil-animate: Build an animation from scratch in the right order: whether to animate, purpose, properties, easing, duration, interruption, exit. Writes the code.
emil-choreograph: Coordinate several elements animating together (stagger, entrances, view swaps) so the group reads as one motion.
emil-design-eng: Emil Kowalski's design-engineering philosophy for UI polish: press and hover states, popovers, transitions, invisible details.
emil-gestures: Build drag, swipe and sheet interactions that track the finger and stay interruptible (drawers, swipe-to-dismiss, reorder).
emil-mobile-native: Make a web app feel native on a phone: tap highlights, 100vh bug, input zoom, notch, pull-to-refresh, status bar.
emil-pick-ui-library: Pick a UI component library for a project. Invoke only on request.
emil-remove-animations: Find and remove animations an interface doesn't need (keyboard actions, high-frequency surfaces, decoration). Subtracts only.
emil-review-animations: Review animation code against a high craft bar: weak easing, wrong origin, layout animation, missing reduced-motion.
excalidraw-board: Turn a task doc, backlog or open questions into a black-and-white Excalidraw discussion board, or read back an edited board.
explainer-deck: Build a slide deck (Google Slides or pptx) explaining how a system or document works, each mechanism drawn with a worked example.
extract-shared-package: Extract a module shared by several apps into a Composer or npm package: boundary, hosting, versioning, CI, rollout.
function-parameter-limits: Apply the 0/2/3+ parameter-count rule: advise wrapping arguments in an object and set up a lint rule.
gchat-format: Convert Markdown to Google Chat formatting for messages, release notes or documents.
hobby-review: Socratic debrief of a finished anime, book or game against the taste rubric in the matching current.md.
judgement: Decide whether a mid-task finding is yours to fix, worth a question, or out of scope; measure who it affects first.
md-to-pdf: Convert Markdown to a PDF with rendered Mermaid diagrams and charts.
merge-task-docs: Find overlapping task docs in a domain, merge them, delete the sources and fix back-references.
motion-clip: Make a short designed product or brand video (launch clip, promo, app preview) written as code and rendered to MP4 in several sizes.
notes-summary: Create, update or read a personal session journal of non-code conversations and decisions.
patch-advisory: Respond to a security advisory: find affected hosts and containers, judge exposure, patch or mitigate, verify, report.
plan-worklist: Turn an already-scoped list of work items into a sized, sequenced build plan before any code is written.
posthog-replay-frames: Find what one user actually did and saw in a PostHog session, from raw events and replay screenshots.
product-still: Make a designed still image from a product's real screens: how-it-works steps, feature or hero images, social cards.
pull-db: Pull a remote MySQL/MariaDB database to local dev, or an allowlist copy without personal data.
quick-done: Cheap wrap-up for a small session: capture lessons and update one task doc, no review.
read-summary: Read the task docs and project instructions for a domain before answering or building, so recorded decisions and gotchas are not missed.
refresh-instructions: Three-pass refresh of any living doc (restructure, condense, unhobble), each pass verified before the next.
reverse-engineer: Study a web app the client already uses and rebuild its mechanism in your own app, with a reviewed write-up before design.
score-loop: Score work against a fixed rubric, fix the gaps, re-score with an independent reviewer, repeat until the target is met.
setup-playwright: Set up or harden a Playwright E2E suite: config, auth, seeded fixtures, parallel-safe data, flaky-test fixes.
setup-project-docs: Establish a project's core docs: PRD, ARCHITECTURE, ARCHITECTURE-ESSENTIALS and AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md.
setup-tools: Set up syafiqkit's Google Sheets, Chat, Gmail and remote-SSH tools on this machine.
setup-tracker: Set up or restructure a shared Google Sheets tracker for client asks, issues and who owes what.
ship: Ship to production: commit, changelog, push, verify CI/CD, release note, close tracker cards. Run after done.
sign-pdf: Sign, initial and date a PDF form with your own signature image and return a checked signed copy.
sweep-doc-overlaps: Scan all task-doc domains for cross-domain overlaps and hand confirmed groups to merge-task-docs.
tackle: Continue a doc with several open items: read it, judge what is buildable, then build it.
task-summary: Create or update task summary docs (current.md plus decisions files): paths, templates, cross-references, Quick Start.
uat-script: Build a client UAT script: test scenarios per role as CSV, rendered to an Excel workbook with status dropdown and summary.
uiux: Design judgement for UI/UX at any scope: polish, redesign, critique, research, go-live check. Measures real renders at several widths.
understanding-guide: Turn long reports or specs into an offline question-and-answer page, every claim checked against its source.
unhobble-instructions: Rewrite an instruction file (skill, agent, CLAUDE.md, command) to separate real constraints from over-strict rules.
update-claude-docs: Create, rewrite or capture lessons into CLAUDE.md files following a best-practice layout.
update-summary: Alias of task-summary: update a task summary with session findings, creating the doc if missing.
user-manual: Write an end-user manual: scope, tutorials, screenshots, Word or PDF editions, or an in-app help centre.
watch-sheets: Watch shared Google Sheets (client tracker, UAT) on a schedule and alert only when something needs your reply.
write-summary: Alias of task-summary: create task documentation when starting new feature work.
test-driven-development: Write the failing test first, then the minimal code, then refactor. Use before implementing any feature or bugfix.
systematic-debugging: Find the root cause before fixing: reproduce, trace, test one hypothesis at a time. Use for any bug, test failure or odd behaviour.
writing-plans: Turn a spec or requirements into a detailed step-by-step implementation plan before touching code.
executing-plans: Carry out a written implementation plan in this session, task by task, with checks and review points.
requesting-code-review: Ask a reviewer subagent to check finished work against the requirements before merging.
receiving-code-review: Handle review feedback with rigour: verify it, clarify unclear items, push back when it is wrong instead of agreeing.
verification-before-completion: Run the real checks and read their output before claiming work is done, fixed or passing.
dispatching-parallel-agents: Split 2+ independent tasks across parallel subagents, one per problem domain, then integrate the results.
api-and-interface-design: Design stable APIs and module boundaries: contracts, error shapes, versioning, backward compatibility.
code-simplification: Simplify code for clarity without changing behaviour. Use when code works but is hard to read.
performance-optimization: Measure first, then fix the real bottleneck across frontend, backend, queries and databases.
git-workflow-and-versioning: Git practice for any change: small commits, branching, resolving conflicts, versioning.
shipping-and-launch: Pre-launch checklist for production: tests, security, performance, accessibility, rollout and rollback.
spec-driven-development: Write a spec before coding when starting a project, feature or significant change that has none.
security-and-hardening: Harden code against vulnerabilities: threat model, input handling, auth, secrets, dependencies, OWASP Top Ten.
code-review-and-quality: Five-axis code review (correctness, readability, architecture, security, performance) before merging a change or PR.
owasp-llm-top10: Security audit of LLM apps against the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications: prompt injection, data leakage, excessive agency.
owasp-ai-testing: AI trustworthiness testing with the OWASP AI Testing Guide: test cases across application, model, infrastructure and data layers.
secpriv-code-review: Single-pass code review for security weaknesses (CWE) and privacy violations (GDPR), precision first. From Meta.
nielsen-heuristics-audit: Usability audit of a screen or flow against Nielsen's 10 heuristics, with severity-rated findings.
wcag-accessibility-audit: Accessibility audit against WCAG 2.1/2.2 (perceivable, operable, understandable, robust) with fixes.
cognitive-walkthrough: Step through a task as a first-time user to find where people would get lost or stuck.
ux-audit-rethink: Holistic UX audit using usability factors and interaction dimensions, ending in prioritised recommendations.
ui-design-review: Visual design review: typography, colour, spacing, hierarchy and consistency.
accessibility-engineering: Audit existing interfaces for WCAG 2.2 AA conformance and fix the violations found.
frontend-ui-engineering: Build production-quality, accessible, responsive user interfaces and components.
documentation-and-adrs: Record architecture decisions (ADRs), update docs when APIs change, and detect docs that drifted from the code.
codebase-documenter: Write documentation of how a codebase works: architecture, key components, data flow, onboarding.
technical-doc-creator: Create HTML technical documentation with code blocks, API workflows, architecture diagrams and syntax highlighting.
remotion-motion-graphics: Create and edit motion-graphics videos with Remotion (React): intros, promos, captions, animated text. Needs Node.
explainer-video: Make a 30-90 second animated explainer: script, storyboard, scenes, narration and captions. Remotion-based.
caption-animation: Animated word-by-word captions from a transcript or SRT, burned into video. Remotion-based.
short-form-video: Make Reels, TikTok or Shorts: hook, pacing, retention, loops and 9:16 safe areas.
audiogram: Turn podcast or voice audio into a waveform video clip for social media.
youtube-intro-outro: Design a YouTube channel intro, logo sting or end card as a reusable template.
talking-head-b-roll: Add motion-graphics b-roll to a talking-head video from its transcript. Needs ffmpeg and Node.
vlog-auto-edit: Automatically edit raw travel or daily footage into a finished vlog using ffmpeg, speech transcription and a vision model.
subagent-driven-development: Execute a written plan by dispatching a fresh subagent per task with review after each. Needs bash (Git Bash on Windows) for its helper scripts.
using-git-worktrees: Create an isolated git worktree before starting feature work or executing a plan, so the main checkout stays clean.
finishing-a-development-branch: When implementation is done and tests pass, decide how to integrate: merge, pull request, keep or discard the branch.
delegate-and-verify: Hand bulk, parallel or mechanical work (30+ files, rows or reports, multi-pass rewrites) to subagents, then verify the results before reporting. Use wherever a skill says to dispatch to haiku.
impeccable: Design director toolkit for any frontend: shape, critique, audit, polish, bolder, quieter, animate, harden. Say "impeccable polish" or "impeccable audit". Original author's Harness build.
taste: Build or redesign a landing page, company or product site so it looks designed, not templated: layout, type, palette, licensed stand-in photos, copy checks, browser finish gate. Needs Node 22+ and Edge or Chrome.
write-a-skill: Write or improve a Harness skill (SKILL.md): where it goes, a description that triggers, a short body, and how to test it.
schedule-checks: Run a check on a repeating schedule (CI, a page, a file, a sheet) and be told only when something needs you, using Harness scheduled tasks.
plan-to-ship: Take a feature from rough idea to reviewed, committed code with human gates: prime, intent, architecture, slices, plan, build, validate, review, retro. Use for any non-trivial change.
harness-check: Audit how well a project is set up for AI agents (instructions, one-command checks, tests that can fail, guardrails, skills, feedback loop), score it and fix the gaps.
prime-codebase: Orient in a codebase before planning or building: structure, docs, entry points, conventions. Run at the start of work in an unfamiliar project.
prime-backend: Orient in a codebase's backend: API routes, services, data layer, tests. Use before backend work.
prime-frontend: Orient in a codebase's frontend: components, routing, state, styling. Use before frontend work.
plan-create-prd: Interview the user into a problem-first PRD (problem, evidence, hypothesis, MVP) that states intent and leaves engineering choices to the architecture step.
plan-architecture: Decide how to build it: explore 2-3 approaches, stack, data shape, boundaries and risks with the user, then write a high-level architecture note.
plan-with-priorities: Plan a decision by first eliciting what matters to the user, then recommend options with small spikes and explicit trade-offs.
plan-create-stories: Turn a PRD into a backlog of stories in GitHub or Jira (needs gh or a tracker connection).
piv-slice-epic: Slice an epic and its architecture into tickets sized for one agent loop, with a dependency graph and what can run in parallel.
piv-plan-implementation: Write a one-pass-ready implementation plan for a ticket or feature: codebase patterns, research, tasks with validation commands, acceptance criteria. No code.
piv-implement: Carry out an implementation plan task by task, running each task's validation, then the full checks, and write a report with deviations.
piv-validate: Run the project's full check suite (tests, types, lint) and return one PASS or FAIL verdict. A template: needs the project's real commands.
piv-review-changes: Review recently changed files for bugs, security issues and standards, and write the findings to a file.
piv-fix-review-findings: Triage review findings with the user, fix the chosen ones one at a time with tests, defer the rest, then validate.
piv-commit: Create one atomic, conventionally tagged git commit for the current changes, without staging secrets. Never pushes.
piv-create-pr: Push the branch and open a pull request with a real body from the plan and report (needs gh; asks before pushing).
piv-review-pr: Review an open pull request with fresh eyes: severity-ranked findings posted to GitHub (needs gh).
piv-investigate-issue: Investigate a GitHub issue in parallel to an evidence-backed root cause analysis (needs gh).
piv-implement-issue: Implement the fix for a GitHub issue from its root cause analysis, with regression tests (needs gh).
worktree-create: Create several git worktrees for parallel work, each on its own branch with config copied, dependencies installed and health-checked.
worktree-merge: Merge branches from parallel worktrees through one integration branch, validating after each.
rules-create-global: Write a lean AGENTS.md (global project rules) derived from the codebase or specs, with recurring detail moved to reference docs.
rules-check-drift: Check whether AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md is still true after recent changes: commands, paths and rules that no longer match.
system-execution-report: After finishing an implementation, record what was done, what diverged from the plan and why.
system-evolution-review: Review how an implementation followed its plan and find bugs in the process: edits to AGENTS.md, plan template or skills.
